findings.issue_text: Google Calendar CalendarService passes the zod SafeParse wrapper from parseRefreshTokenResponse directly into prisma.credential.update instead of the parsed .data, corrupting the credential key (access_token becomes undefined) on every token refresh

parseRefreshTokenResponse's minimum schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` which both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", overwriting each other so the schema never validates an expiry field or permits real provider properties

zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId to refreshOAuthTokens where every other call site passes credential.userId, sending the wrong calcomUserId to the credential sync endpoint and returning another user's tokens

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response for all apps when credential sync is enabled, but callers (Google, HubSpot, Zoho CRM/Bigin) expect provider-shaped objects, breaking at runtime; the `any` return type hides the mismatch from TypeScript
parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" into the credential when the provider response has no refresh_token, persisting a bogus token on the non-sync path too
salesforce CalendarService checks `response.statusText !== "OK"` to detect failure, but statusText is empty on HTTP/2, so every successful Salesforce refresh throws; should check response.ok/status

salesforce CalendarService performs an unconditional refresh-token network call plus prisma.credential.update on every service construction with no isExpired check, adding latency and rate-limit risk to every booking/availability path
app-credential webhook compares the webhook secret with `!==`, a non-constant-time comparison, instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual over fixed-length buffers
app-credential webhook has no HTTP method check and no try/catch, so schema.parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse throw raw errors producing unhandled 500s instead of 400s

refreshOAuthTokens POSTs to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no authentication header, no Content-Type, and never checks the response status, so error bodies are returned to callers as token payloads

zoomvideo and office365video VideoApiAdapters hardcode appSlug strings ("zoomvideo", "msteams", "lark-calendar", "office365-calendar") instead of reading the slug from each app's config.json, causing slug mismatches with the sync endpoint and app-credential webhook lookup
`.env.example` comment says the key must be 32 bytes for AES256 but the suggested command `openssl rand -base64 24` produces 24 random bytes, contradicting the stated requirement

No tests accompany the new app-credential webhook, parseRefreshTokenResponse, or refreshOAuthTokens, despite these being deterministic credential-writing paths where silent corruption is the failure mode
salesforce CalendarService's `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is dead code because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on failure

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED in packages/lib/constants.ts is typed `string | undefined` holding the raw encryption key secret rather than being coerced to boolean with `!!(...)`, risking secret leakage into a client bundle

office365calendar CalendarService removed the console.error containing the zod error and raw MS response, replacing it with a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" throw that leaves Outlook refresh failures undiagnosable

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook compares the webhook secret with `!==`, a non-constant-time comparison, instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual over fixed-length buffers

adjudication.rationale:
In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret is validated via a direct inequality check:

```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```

This is a normal string comparison and is not constant-time. For secret/token validation, this can enable timing side-channels (even if practically difficult over a network), whereas `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over fixed-length buffers is the standard mitigation. The issue is directly present in the diff and is not speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens POSTs to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT with no authentication header, no Content-Type, and never checks the response status, so error bodies are returned to callers as token payloads

adjudication.rationale: In the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` with no explicit authentication headers and no explicit `Content-Type` header. It also does not check `response.ok` / status codes and simply returns the raw `Response` to callers. This is verifiable in the diff. As a result, callers can proceed with a non-2xx response without the helper stopping it (and some call sites assume a token-like result), so the core concern about missing status checking (and missing auth headers) is a real issue introduced here, though the "error bodies are returned as token payloads" part is somewhat overstated because the helper returns an unparsed `Response` rather than a parsed body.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zoomvideo and office365video VideoApiAdapters hardcode appSlug strings ("zoomvideo", "msteams", "lark-calendar", "office365-calendar") instead of reading the slug from each app's config.json, causing slug mismatches with the sync endpoint and app-credential webhook lookup

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce hardcoded `appSlug` string literals passed into `refreshOAuthTokens` (e.g., "msteams", "lark-calendar", "office365-calendar", "google-calendar", "hubspot"). However, the proposed finding claims this will cause slug mismatches because it should be read from each app’s `config.json`, and it specifically mentions `zoomvideo` (not shown/changed in this diff). From the diff alone, there is no evidence that these literals do not match the actual app slugs used elsewhere (e.g., the webhook handler looks up apps by `slug` and uses `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]`). Therefore the asserted mismatch/defect is not verifiable from this diff and is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.env.example` comment says the key must be 32 bytes for AES256 but the suggested command `openssl rand -base64 24` produces 24 random bytes, contradicting the stated requirement

adjudication.rationale: In `.env.example` the new section for `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` states "must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm" but immediately suggests generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which produces 24 random bytes (then base64-encodes them). That contradicts the stated 32-byte requirement and would mislead users into generating a too-short key if the code truly expects 32 bytes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests accompany the new app-credential webhook, parseRefreshTokenResponse, or refreshOAuthTokens, despite these being deterministic credential-writing paths where silent corruption is the failure mode

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new runtime code paths (a webhook handler and OAuth token refresh helpers) but does not add any accompanying test files or test changes. While the absence of tests is verifiable from the diff, it is not itself a concrete bug, security flaw, or correctness defect introduced by the code changes; it is a process/coverage concern rather than a functional problem demonstrable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED in packages/lib/constants.ts is typed `string | undefined` holding the raw encryption key secret rather than being coerced to boolean with `!!(...)`, risking secret leakage into a client bundle

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not touch `packages/lib/constants.ts` or show how `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined/typed, so the claim that it is `string | undefined` and “holding the raw encryption key secret” cannot be verified from the changes shown. In this diff, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is only imported and used as a boolean-like guard in server-side code paths; there is no demonstrated secret value being assigned to it, nor any demonstrated client-bundle export/leakage introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar CalendarService removed the console.error containing the zod error and raw MS response, replacing it with a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned" throw that leaves Outlook refresh failures undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous logic did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and, on failure, executed a `console.error(...)` that included both the Zod error and the raw Microsoft token response (`responseJson`). The diff replaces this with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, and that helper throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure without logging/including the Zod error or the MS response. This is a verifiable regression in diagnostics/observability for Outlook token refresh failures introduced by the change.
